A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TH2T research work. All 21 pages of v1 and 19 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original TH2T experiments, including accuracy, token length, latency, generalization results, ablations, and reasoning-structure analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original TH2T results and adds GPQA evaluations, Llama-model experiments, and performance breakdowns by difficulty.

M1.justification: The specified Stage-2 redundancy Determinator changes from DeepSeek-R1 in v1 Section 4.2 to GPT-4 in v2 Methodology. The two-stage framework, difficulty prefixes, redundancy truncation, synthetic looping, and optional probe otherwise retain the same substantive procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds actual evaluation on GPQA, extending coverage beyond v1's four mathematical benchmarks to question answering. Figure 5 and appendix Table 5 provide results for this additional domain.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds TokenSkip results to the 7B and 14B MATH-500 comparisons, where v1 provided no entries. The other named comparators remain D-Prompt, NoThinking, and CoT-Valve. Both versions attribute the fine-tuning baselines' results to their source papers, so expanded participation does not establish new baseline runs.

E3.justification: v2 adds R1-Distill-Llama-8B experiments and evaluation by finer difficulty subsets, including OmniMath levels 7–8. Existing Qwen settings, training-set size, and decoding limits are retained. Stage-2 composition wording changes from modifying 50% of D1 to a 1:1 redundancy/looping split, but v2 still says only part of D1 is modified; the actual intervention fraction remains unclear.

E4.justification: New appendix Figure 7 examines whether accuracy and length savings persist across problem-difficulty levels. Existing stage ablations, starting-model comparisons, training-progress analysis, reasoning-structure statistics, and three case studies remain. The expanded starting-model table redisplays existing R1 results rather than establishing another ablation.

E5.justification: v2's appendix newly specifies a fixed random seed of 42. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. The seed disclosure does not establish additional runs.

E6.justification: v2 substantially expands results with GPQA evaluations, the five-benchmark Llama table, and difficulty-stratified findings. Table 1 revises baseline values: for example, CoT-Valve's reported 7B GSM8K accuracy delta changes from −1.00 to −3.61 points. Table 2 changes TH2T's easy-OmniMath difficulty-cognition score from 90.0% to 96.7%. Main TH2T Table 1 results are retained apart from displayed precision; revised imported baseline values do not establish controlled same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: The dataset definitions, reasoning-chunk representation, and hypnosis/truncation formulations retain their mathematical substance. Splitting equations, distinguishing hypnosis symbols, and moving trigger text into prose are presentational changes. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v2's conclusion adds an explicit first-to-inject claim for difficulty, redundancy, and looping hypnosis as built-in reasoning triggers. The central two-stage contribution and headline claims of substantial length reduction with maintained performance remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly argues that internal triggers offer flexibility, robustness, and better instruction following, and interprets reduced reflection as suggesting extensive reflection is unnecessary for strong reasoning. Its limitations add correctness-ratio sampling as a possible model-specific difficulty measure while identifying its computational cost. Existing capability-boundary and RL-resource limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 identifies Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct as the additional short-CoT data generator and revises the disclosed redundancy-labeling implementation to GPT-4. Existing prompt templates, LoRA hyperparameters, hardware, and generation limits are retained, largely relocated to More Experimental Details. No new code or data access instructions appear.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for GPQA, Llama 3, and GPT-4, while removing the LoRA and causally motivated sycophancy references. It adds an explicit priority claim and removes the earlier passage acknowledging similar built-in triggers. The broader efficient-reasoning literature organization and positioning remain substantially intact.

P1.justification: v2 extensively condenses and rewrites the abstract, literature review, methodology, and experimental narrative. Numbered sections become unnumbered headings, stage terminology is revised, and the appendix is reorganized around experimental details and results before motivation, prompts, limitations, and cases.

P2.justification: The paper changes from single-column to predominantly two-column layout. The baseline plot moves to the opening page and is redrawn; Table 1 separates gains, reductions, and speedups into columns; reflection and looping tables are merged. Training-progress plots move to the appendix and become separate panels, while new Llama and difficulty displays and GPQA panels are added.

improvement.justification: GPQA and Llama evaluations broaden the empirical support beyond v1's Qwen mathematical experiments, while the difficulty breakdown directly examines the paper's central adaptation claim. The revised ablation deltas also agree with Table 1's printed reduction percentages. These gains support a limited overall improvement, tempered by unclear provenance for the expanded absolute baseline results and unresolved Stage-2 data-mixture wording.
